_about: Catalog overrides for the `correspondence` register. Inherits _base; this file
only records the differences.
WHY THESE TWO ARE OFF, added 2026-08-04.
`assistant-preamble` and `chatbot-register` catch the assistant's conversational
moves: offering to do more, hoping this helps, asking whether there is anything
else. In an encyclopedia article those are dispositive. In an email they are
Tuesday — 'let me know if you need anything else before Friday' is a sign-off,
not a tell.
Both entries shipped in Tier A, which bypasses density gating and carries the
acceptance gate's absolute zero-false-positives rule. So an ordinary polite email
tripped the tier whose entire claim is that it does not do that.
It went unnoticed because the acceptance corpus is 45 documents of encyclopedic
prose. It cannot exercise this register at all, so '0 of 12 human documents' was
measuring somewhere the failure could not occur. Clean on the corpus you have is
not the same as clean.
Disabled here rather than deleted, because the signal is real in the registers
these entries were written for — an article that offers to expand its own section
has one explanation. `model-self-identification` stays ON in every register,
because no human describes themselves as a large language model.
See CALIBRATION.md FP-2026-08-04-d.
